Definition: from G303 and G1166; to exhibit, i.e. (by implication) to indicate, appoint:--appoint, shew.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to show, or to appoint: after these things the Lord appointed other seventy also and sent them two and two before His face, and the disciples prayed, 'Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men, shew whether of these two thou hast chosen.' It is God pointing at the one He has picked — the seventy sent out, and Matthias shown to take Judas's place.
TheologicalSignificance: Two verses about appointing carry no doctrine of their own; their weight is the choosing — the Lord appoints the seventy, and the Lord shows which man He has chosen.
